speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when you were first noticed by emergency services?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reported immediate pain in both knees and severe right groin pain; did you notice any specific deformity, such as the right leg appearing shortened or externally rotated, upon arrival at the scene?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right-sided hip dislocation.

The clinical presentation of severe right groin pain with the leg shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated is classic for a posterior hip dislocation. Given the history of a rear-end collision, I need to confirm neurological status and rule out associated fractures.

REQUEST TEST: Right hip X-ray AP and Frog-leg view.
REQUEST TEST: Right lower extremity neurological exam (motor and sensory).
